note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after the userns conversion. The unit's only change since the last verdict is userns.Enter(t) as its first statement (the child re-runs the whole body in its own user, network and mount namespace; a child failure or skip propagates to the parent, and a child that ran nothing fails it) plus removal of EPERM/EACCES skips, so a refused privilege now fails instead of skipping. Assertions are byte-identical. Section 4.4: 'All IS-IS routers are therefore required to transmit and receive ISO 9542 ISH packets on point-to-point links.' TestRFC1195ISHVethTransport runs the production AF_PACKET transport at both ends of a veth pair, sends an ISH with NET and protocols-supported through SendISH, and fails unless the peer's circuit receives it addressed to AllESs with the identical PDU and decodes NET and holding time. The capability error from HandleLinkUp is now fatal, not a skip. Root units unchanged: TestRFC1195ISHTransmitReceive (ISH before first IIH, received ISH initializes peer), TestRFC1195NeighborWithoutISHStillFormsAdjacency (negative), corruption/wrong-circuit and password units as supplementary negatives. The veth unit's own revert record of SendISH, owed per the earlier verdict, is not claimed here.
